decisions.reason: Although technically close to the core wafer business, this older specialized product appears to have lost visibility and is plausibly being superseded by the firm's newer flagship interposer and packaging-wafer developments.
Carrier wafers are a low-risk extension of the firm's established thin-wafer handling offer and remain well aligned with its stated direction toward reusable carriers and process support substrates.
As a flagship 2019 launch in advanced glass interposer technology, it fits the firm's R&D-intensive semiconductor packaging strategy and would typically be given more time to build demand.
The off-the-shelf glass and quartz wafer brand is close to the firm's core capabilities, broadens commercialization of standard products, and carries relatively little technical or strategic risk.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's narrow precision-wafer focus, so management would likely reallocate resources away from this weaker strategic fit toward core substrate and packaging products.
